HP 12 D 9174 going ahead applied sudden brake which was reciprocated by driver of car bearing no. DL2CP 8151 which was being driven diligently by maintaining safe driving distance and slowed down safety without striking any vehicle going ahead, suddenly within a spur of a second truck no, RJ 29GA 4388 coming from behind hit the rear portion of the Wagon R Car. texts.arguments: Rakesh Sehgal Vs. Mukul Kumar & Ors. stated that the present petition should be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties i.e. driver, owner and insurance company of vehicle no. HP 12 D 9174. 8. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has argued that in the case in hand, the charge-sheet pertaining to FIR No. 263/2019 PS Butana Karnal U/s 279/337/304 A IPC was registered against the respondent No.1 and from this, it is established that he was driving the offending offending rashly and negligently at the time of accident. 27. The petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 who is also the eye witness and PW1 has reiterated and reaffirmed the stand that the accident in question was caused on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1. 28. The respondents no.1 and 2 have not led any evidence to prove that the accident in question was not taken RAKESH In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors (2009) 13 SC 530, in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, 2001 ACJ 421 SC, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as 2009 ACJ 287, it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Rakesh Sehgal vs Mukul Kumar @ Mukul Singh Gurjar And Ors on 8 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153952187/ 10 30. In Rajwati @ Rajjo Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited (2022) (SC) 1016, it has been held as under:- "In a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial. The Court must keep this distinction in mind. As held by this court in Sunita (supra) and Kusum Lata (supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e. to say, 'the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases." Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be appropriate to look into the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its division bench decision in matter of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors." (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held : - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) RAKESH Digitally signed by RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2023.11.30 13:14:56 +0530 Rakesh Sehgal Vs. Mukul Kumar & Ors. (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim.
